findings.reason: the worker reaches a refusal on the third case with no stated way out and must either invent an unstated member drop or stop, so the fixture needs to say the write retires a roster member (register one, then retire it) before `commit=True` can reach the branch.
findings.text: §2's third case cannot run as written: `write(commit=True)` names a roster retirement, and `reckon/ledger.py:2135-2139` raises `LedgerError("nothing to commit for …: commit=True names the roster rows a write dropped, and this write dropped none")` before any per-run file is touched, while the fixture the section describes holds "a ledger and one per-run record" with no member to drop, so the case asserts a commit that is never made and its negative control ("doing so in `write`'s commit branch leaves it modified in the third") has no write to leave modified

findings.reason: the guard belongs where the request line is composed, in `_request_host_follower`, which both writers share; as written the worker may ship a check the reproduced path never reaches and §1's misplacement survives it.
findings.text: §3 puts the ownership guard in `_ask_session_host_for_follower` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:770`), but that is not the only writer of a follow request: `_hand_off_from_follower` (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:625`) reaches `_hand_off_to_waiting_host` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:870`), which calls `_request_host_follower` directly, so a hand-armed follower of another session's run that hands its pair to a waiting host writes the misdirected request without passing the new check — and the section names no production caller of either path, so nothing in it shows which path the reproduced misdirection takes
